title: Netflix’s Latest Move Is a Huge Win for Travelers
summary: Netflix announced a major expansion, launching in 130 new countries and bringing its total availability to 190 countries globally. This move, dubbed "the birth of a global Internet TV network" by CEO Reed Hastings, makes Netflix accessible in most parts of the world, excluding China, Crimea, North Korea, and Syria. The company also plans to release two dozen original films and documentaries, new kids' series, and stand-up comedy specials in 2016.

title: Netflix expands into 130 more countries, including Malta, in surprise move
summary: Netflix has unexpectedly expanded its service to 130 additional countries, including Malta, bringing its total reach to 190 countries. This move, announced by CEO Reed Hastings at CES, significantly accelerates Netflix's global expansion plans, though it still faces challenges in entering China and certain other markets due to restrictions or language barriers. The expansion delighted investors, with Netflix's stock climbing, as it positions the company to attract millions of new subscribers and further invest in its growing library of original programming, while a local provider, Melita, welcomes the service to Malta.

title: Microsoft Surface Pro 4 finally arrives in India at a starting price of Rs 89,990
summary: Microsoft has officially launched the Surface Pro 4 and the older Surface Pro 3 in India, with the Surface Pro 4 starting at Rs 89,990. The devices are available for pre-order exclusively through Amazon.in, with deliveries commencing from January 14. Microsoft has also established experience centers in major Indian cities for product demonstrations.

title: Gates and Bezos partner with Sloan Kettering for controversial cancer treatment
summary: Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos are partnering with Sloan Kettering to back Grail, a startup focused on detecting cancer. This collaboration comes at a time when technologies like liquid biopsies and gene-sequencing are becoming more affordable and viable for screening at-risk patients. The initiative aims to advance cancer detection methods.

title: Netflix revolution hits Malta
summary: Netflix expanded into 130 new countries, including Malta, marking a significant global push. CEO Reed Hastings announced this "birth of a global TV network" at CES, surprising many investors and generating an increase in Netflix's stock price. Maltese TV provider Melita welcomed Netflix's entry, viewing it as a positive development for customer choice and an incentive for users to upgrade internet packages for optimal streaming.

title: Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates bet on blood tests for cancer
summary: Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates have invested in Grail, a startup spun out of Illumina Inc., which aims to detect multiple cancers early through a single blood test. The company announced over $100 million in Series A funding led by Illumina and ARCH Venture Partners, with participation from Bezos Expeditions, Microsoft cofounder Gates, and Sutter Hill Ventures. This venture seeks to revolutionize cancer detection, despite potential profitability challenges.

title: G.E. Is Moving Headquarters to Boston and Itself Into the Digital Era
summary: General Electric announced it is moving its global headquarters from Fairfield, Connecticut, to Boston, Massachusetts. This move signifies G.E.'s strategic transformation into a digital industrial company, aiming to embed itself within a thriving technology and academic ecosystem. The relocation underscores the broader trend of old-line companies re-evaluating their strategies to adapt to the digital era.

title: Meet Symphony, the Company That Tracks Netflix's Elusive Ratings
summary: Symphony Advanced Media is a Palo Alto-based company that tracks viewership data for streaming services like Netflix and Amazon, which typically keep their numbers secret. Using an app with audio recognition technology, Symphony's VideoPulse service gathers data from a panel of 15,000 mobile device users to estimate program viewership. This provides an unofficial metric for content consumption on streaming platforms, addressing a frustration among TV executives regarding the lack of transparency in streaming viewership numbers.

title: ING moving farther south on Sixth Avenue
summary: ING Financial Holdings Corp. is relocating its office 10 blocks south on Sixth Avenue, signing a 10-year lease for 132,400 square feet at 1133 Sixth Avenue. The move will place the company in the same building as a new Steinway & Sons piano showroom. This new location was previously considered by Amazon, but Durst Organization has a pending fraud claim against the tech giant for backing out of that deal.

title: Amazon Reveals New Details About Drone Deliveries
summary: Amazon has revealed new details about its Prime Air drone delivery service, aiming for 30-minute deliveries for packages up to five pounds. The drones will be capable of traveling over 10 miles and are designed to avoid obstacles, akin to how a horse avoids a tree. While regulatory hurdles remain, Amazon envisions drone deliveries becoming as common as delivery trucks in the future, with features like noise dampening being addressed.

title: Israeli DevOps startup JFrog raises $50m
summary: Israeli DevOps startup JFrog has successfully raised $50 million in a new funding round from several investors including Scale Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Battery Ventures. These funds will be used for talent acquisition, technological advancements, and global expansion to meet the increasing demand for their DevOps and software automation platform. JFrog, known for its Artifactory and Bintray products, aims to further lead the market with enhanced solutions that are 10x better than single-technology offerings from competitors.

title: IBM, Symantec storage results bode ill for EMC, HPE
summary: Recent fourth-quarter results from IBM's storage business and Symantec's Veritas unit show significant year-over-year revenue declines, painting a bleak picture for the storage market. These negative results suggest potential challenges for industry leaders EMC and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), which are expected to report their earnings soon. Despite analysts' expectations for modest growth from EMC, the observed market contraction by IBM and Symantec indicates that EMC might struggle to meet these targets, especially as hardware makers face increasing competition from cloud service providers.

title: Why the Charter–Time Warner Cable Merger is a Bad Deal (Guest Column)
summary: This guest column argues that the proposed merger between Charter Communications, Time Warner Cable, and Bright House Networks is detrimental to competition and innovation, particularly in the high-speed broadband market. The authors, from the Writers Guild of America, West, contend that it would leave two companies, Comcast and the new Charter entity, controlling nearly 90% of the market, enabling them to stifle online video competition and limit consumer choice. They highlight the potential for these merged entities to manipulate internet service pricing, impose data caps, and control accessible online content, ultimately reversing the progress made in online video distribution.

title: Trend Lifts Auto-Parts Demand; AutoZone, O'Reilly Near Highs
summary: The demand for auto parts is rising due to several market trends including low gasoline prices encouraging more driving, and the increasing average age of cars leading to more repairs. AutoZone's stock is performing well despite recent market pullbacks, benefiting from these trends that are boosting auto-parts retailers.
